fields.question: Why maintain a quality–diversity archive per EliteReplay problem?
fields.answer: Accuracy alone can shrink solution coverage. Keep the shortest verified solution per approach/structure cell to preserve distinct successful strategies rather than store ordinary IID replay.
fields.example: Separate algebra and geometry cells so the common strategy doesn't overwrite the other.

fields.question: How does shortest-per-cell MAP-Elites differ from a global shortest answer?
fields.answer: Cell-local replacement preserves other strategies. Store actual descriptors, not requested approaches, which may not match generated behavior.
fields.example: A proof requested as induction but generated by enumeration belongs to the enumeration cell.

fields.question: Why balance problems before occupied cells?
fields.answer: Otherwise larger archives dominate replay. Average response tokens, mix archive and GRPO as specified, clear padding before exponentiating and use no test gold for archiving.
fields.example: More occupied cells should not give one problem ten times the sampling weight.

fields.question: Why index EliteReplay by realized approach and balance problem before cell?
fields.answer: Requested methods can differ from generated ones. Use actual descriptor and retain shortest verified answer in each cell. Problem-first balancing prevents archive size from allocating weight. This isn't IID success caching.
fields.example: A requested geometry solution using algebra belongs in algebra, or identical methods masquerade as diversity.

fields.question: Why mask a valid premise in CCE's teacher contrast?
fields.answer: A teacher may follow a mistaken student prefix instead of using conditions. Matched ablation reveals condition-sensitive directions for an extrapolated auxiliary target. Student always sees the full problem.
fields.example: Removing a numerical premise can identify which next tokens depend on it.

fields.question: Does disabling CCE auxiliary gating remove all OPD at a position?
fields.answer: No. Sampled PPO-OPD remains; only auxiliary forward KL is removed. Premise eligibility and entropy gate the extra term.
fields.example: A low-entropy format token still receives base distillation.

fields.question: Where is CCE entropy computed, and is student renormalized on support?
fields.answer: Compute entropy on full teacher vocabulary before top-set union. Normalize auxiliary target within support but preserve student full softmax for outside-support gradients. Denominator counts all valid positions.
fields.example: Student support renormalization would hide outside mass and change loss.

fields.question: Why match student prefixes across views and keep full student normalization?
fields.answer: Fixed prefixes isolate premise removal. Teacher auxiliary target is normalized on candidate support but student uses full-vocabulary softmax, retaining outside gradients. Gate controls only auxiliary correction; base OPD stays.
fields.example: If premise and student reasoning both change, likelihood differences can't isolate the premise.

fields.question: Why require note-induced replays to improve RSHD pass rate?
fields.answer: Plausible reflection may not improve behavior. Independently resample and accept only strict improvement over original group, then distill new continuations rather than old failures.
fields.example: A note suggesting unit checks is rejected if retries still all fail.

fields.question: How does uniform replay selection differ from keeping successes only?
fields.answer: Uniform selection preserves the note-induced distribution. Success-only conditions on outcomes a second time after note-level gating and changes provenance.
fields.example: An accepted replay group can include failures; don't silently retain only the correct answer.

fields.question: Do zero-lift RSHD tokens count in the auxiliary denominator?
fields.answer: Yes. Count all valid accepted replay tokens, including zeros. No accepted note gives exactly zero auxiliary loss. Detach teacher/lift and never construct notes from gold.
fields.example: Dividing only by positive-lift count would overamplify sparse weights.

fields.question: Why generate fresh replays and require improvement rather than distill old failures?
fields.answer: Verify the note with actual new behavior and a strict pass-rate gain. Uniformly sample accepted replays and compare note/no-note positive lift on identical prefixes. Old failures aren't fixed by explanation; no gold in notes and no auxiliary term without acceptance.
fields.example: A convincing postmortem with all-failed new attempts is not valid teacher guidance.

fields.question: Why create LoOPSD teachers by repeating layers rather than using bigger weights?
fields.answer: Shared parameters can compute a better distribution through a longer loop. Search contiguous repeat regions and distill on student prefixes. Extra compute, not external answers, supplies guidance.
fields.example: Repeating middle layers changes per-token computation without adding parameters.

fields.question: How does re-searching loops each round differ from a fixed initial loop?
fields.answer: Student updates can change useful repeat regions. Search adapts, and continue only if independent validation beats standard routing, not test-selected routes.
fields.example: A useful repeated middle region can stop helping after the student learns it.

fields.question: Do teacher weights/routes get gradients during LoOPSD distillation?
fields.answer: Freeze both for the round; update standard student via RKL. Training references can be used only for permitted route search, not student rollout. Count repeated-layer compute.
fields.example: Five repeated layers are not free even without new parameters.

fields.question: Why does repeated-layer LoOPSD cost compute and need validation route selection?
fields.answer: Loops change distribution without new weights but execute more layers per token and search multiple routes. Select validation improvements over standard route, then distill student prefixes; never choose on test. More compute doesn't guarantee gains.
fields.example: Rereading a chapter may help but takes time; choose using practice tasks, not final exam answers.

fields.question: Why query unrouted teachers in Road-MOPD?
fields.answer: Shared parameters can degrade other domains even if examples route separately. Evaluate other teachers on the same prefixes for compatibility and real auxiliary gradients.
fields.example: Math updates can affect code behavior despite separate data routing.

fields.question: Can Road token gating replace gradient projection?
fields.answer: No. Gating scales local supervision; projection handles shared-parameter conflict with a target norm floor. A weight formula isn't the complete mechanism.
fields.example: Compatible scores do not rule out gradient conflict.

fields.question: Why not remove the entire conflicting component in Road projection?
fields.answer: Choose maximum feasible projection while preserving the target norm floor; full projection can violate it. Compute actual auxiliary gradients, not static scores or registry labels.
fields.example: Near antiparallel gradients can make a fully projected update vanish.

fields.question: Why use unrouted teachers and impose a target gradient norm floor?
fields.answer: Auxiliary teachers check cross-domain harm on identical states. Gate token credit, then address real gradient conflicts without overweakening target learning. Norm floors are tradeoffs, not universal gains; arbitrary vectors don't replace objectives.
fields.example: Code guidance can protect prefixes during math updates, but full removal might stall math learning.

fields.question: Why align decoded spans for cross-tokenizer CAST?
fields.answer: Token IDs and boundaries differ. Match equivalent decoded spans, then project teacher span logp into student positions.
fields.example: Two Chinese tokenizations may split a word differently but decode to the same span.

fields.question: How does CAST allocation differ from CSD shared events?
fields.answer: CAST distributes total teacher span credit over student positions. CSD builds common-event probability distributions with REST. They conserve different objects.
fields.example: Conserving one span's advantage is not preserving all event probability mass.

fields.question: How does CAST uncertainty weighting preserve chunk credit?
fields.answer: Normalize weights from uncertainty and local smoothness, then multiply chunk total advantage. Anchor unmatched positions to initial student rather than drop them and claim full coverage.
fields.example: A higher token share must not increase total chunk advantage.

fields.question: Why align decoded spans before projecting teacher log probabilities?
fields.answer: Position-wise IDs lack a common event. Verified text spans provide corresponding regions, then uncertainty/smoothness allocate conserved credit. Anchor unmatched text and disclose alignment gaps.
fields.example: If one teacher token becomes several student tokens, verify identical decoded span before allocating its score.
